Through experimentation, practice, or mentorship, you have learned new methods of battle. Fighting Stances each introduce their own benefits and deficits, but only while in use. Knowing when to enter or exit them is key to a successful battle.

You know 2 Fighting Stances from the Stance List below. So long as you meet a known stance’s requirements, you can enter a Fighting Stance either before taking an action on your first turn in combat, after an attack action, or as a minor action.

You automatically exit and are unable to enter Fighting Stances while you do not meet the stance’s requirements, are @Compendium[undertaking.conditions.RK3DF56CKMQUV6DM]{Prone}, @Compendium[undertaking.conditions.PEDR1J13VZXKUF3C]{Stunned}, or @Compendium[undertaking.conditions.9KB959MRZ0H4IT4C]{Unconscious}, or sheathe, drop, or lose possession of the weapon required by the stance. If you exit a stance instead of swapping to another, you retain the stance’s Cons until the start of your next turn.
If a stance requires a weapon trait, all wielded weapons must share that trait. Shields and natural weapons do not count against this, but they also do not gain the stance’s Pros unless they also have the weapon trait(s) required by the stance.

Learning New Stances: You learn 2 more stances at each Growth Level.
Martial Archetypes typically have expanded Fighting Stance options that either become immediately available, or are added to the list of stances you can learn at each Growth Level.
